principles: A gate relaxation must be structurally impossible to trigger without the fact it relaxes for
Prefer wiring a capability that already exists over building a parallel one
A check must read the property it guarantees, not a proxy for it
Where the framework cannot prove something mechanically, say so as a defect rather than accepting prose in its place
drivers: withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom exists, is tested, and has no production caller - the capability is built but unwired
It takes the decision record as input and enforces confirmed + userConfirmed, so backing is structural rather than remembered
core/checklist-status.ts is the tempting route and is the dangerous one: 11 consumers, zero decisionRef awareness
A withdrawal decided during REVIEW is B-1909's own stated trigger, and is exactly the granularity left unwired
The current workaround is three waiver rows whose own text says the framework could not do this mechanically - which stopped being true when B-1909 landed the helper

options.name: A-wire-existing-helper
pros: Uses a decision-backed helper that already exists and is already covered by a smoke
Backing is structural: the function cannot be satisfied by a status string because it never reads one
Mutates nothing - no binding changes, PLAN freeze preserved
Both gates stay strict for every item that is not withdrawn
cons: Wires two hand-named files, which is the same method that left them unwired in the first place
Requires separate anti-bypass proof, since 'it uses the right helper' is a claim until executed

options.name: B-status-predicate
pros: Reuses core/checklist-status.ts, the module built for withdrawal semantics
cons: FATAL: checklist-status.ts has zero decisionRef awareness, so this ships a gate anyone bypasses by writing status='withdrawn' into a JSON file
Turns a correct-but-inconvenient gate into a back door - strictly worse than the bug
Included here because it is the intuitive fix and must be recorded as rejected, not silently avoided

options.name: C-mutate-binding
pros: Removes the demand at its source rather than skipping it at the gate
cons: The affected binding covered a withdrawn AND a delivered item, so whole-binding withdrawal drops real coverage
proofstory_contract_set is PLAN-frozen by deliberate B-1909 design; unfreezing it to satisfy a gate inverts the intended direction
Already refused in practice on B-8df9

options.name: D-derive-consumers
pros: Prevents the fourth recurrence of the enumeration defect rather than fixing the third instance
cons: A codebase-wide audit, not a gate fix; the exclusion triage is the bulk of the work
Does not unblock B-8df9, which is the reason this story exists now
Better as its own story, and is tracked as one

rationale: Option B is the one worth arguing against, because it is what a hurried implementer will actually write: it is a two-line change in the module explicitly built for withdrawal semantics. It is rejected because that module has zero decisionRef awareness, so the resulting skip keys on a string any editor can write - converting a gate that is currently merely inconvenient into one that is bypassable by anyone with file access. That is strictly worse than the defect. The execution boundary therefore blocks core/checklist-status.ts as a path, so the tempting route is mechanically closed rather than merely discouraged. Option A is chosen because the safety property is structural rather than procedural: withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom takes the DECISION RECORD as input and calls decisionAuthorizesWithdrawal, which requires confirmed + userConfirmed, and it never inspects a checklist item at all - so there is no way to satisfy it with a status field. C was already refused in practice on B-8df9 and would have dropped delivered coverage. D is the right long-term answer to recurrence and is tracked separately; folding it in would widen a narrow gate fix into a codebase audit and would not unblock B-8df9.

preMortem.scenario: An implementer ships the naive status check anyway and the words of the checklist are technically satisfied
preMortem.trigger: CHK-002 or CHK-003 lands with `item.status === 'withdrawn'` guarding the skip
preMortem.consequence: The gate becomes bypassable by editing one JSON field - a back door shipped as a bug fix
preMortem.mitigation: core/checklist-status.ts is a BLOCKED path in the execution boundary; CHK-004 exists solely to prove unbacked withdrawals skip nothing, and must be written so a naive implementation fails it

preMortem.scenario: CHK-004's anti-bypass cases are written but are all unreachable via the sanctioned CLI, so they prove nothing about the real threat
preMortem.trigger: Every case is constructed through scope_shrinkage_decision_set, which validates at write time
preMortem.consequence: The anti-bypass proof becomes theatre and the real threat - direct JSON edits - stays untested
preMortem.mitigation: Construct the unbacked states by writing the JSON directly, which IS the threat model; the decision='rejected' overwrite case is additionally CLI-reachable and covers the sanctioned path

preMortem.scenario: CHK-001's repro is built against a fixture whose shape differs from the real B-8df9 case and passes for the wrong reason
preMortem.trigger: The fixture withdraws an item that does NOT share an acceptance binding with a delivered item
preMortem.consequence: The gate might skip it for an unrelated reason and the repro would go green after a fix that does not address the real case
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-001 requires the withdrawn item to SHARE a binding with a delivered item, mirroring B-8df9's AB-002, plus both positive and negative controls

preMortem.scenario: Deleting B-8df9's waivers desynchronises that story's evidence and forces it through another full review round
preMortem.trigger: CHK-005 edits B-8df9's checklist.json while B-8df9 sits in REVIEW in its own worktree
preMortem.consequence: B-8df9 needs a re-attestation round it would not otherwise have needed, or worse, its owner lease rejects the write
preMortem.mitigation: Do it from B-8df9's own worktree with its session id, expect a re-attestation round there regardless since main will have moved, and verify both gates pass with zero waivers before declaring the item done
